Lastly heard on 27.08.2026 Pronounced on 28.08.2026
The petitioner is in custody in connection with Dhalbhumgarh P.S.
Case No. 09 of 2026, for the offences registered under Sections 75
(2)/351 of the B.N.S. 2023 and section 8/10 of the POCSO Act,
pending in the court of learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, at
Jamshedpur.
2. It is submitted that the arrest of the petitioner is vitiated on
account of violation of Article 22 (1) of the Constitution of India. The
grounds of arrest have not been provided to the petitioner and he has
been arrested on 28.03.2026, his detention is ex-facie illegal and
therefore the petitioner maybe released on bail.
3. Reliance has been placed upon the judgment passed by the
Hon’ble Supreme Court reported in (2026) 1 SCC 500 (Mihir Rajesh
Shah versus State of Maharashtra and another), paragraph 37,44,46,
47 and 66 of the said judgment which are quoted as under: -
37. The mandate contained in Article 22(1) of the Constitution of India
is unambiguous and clear in nature, it provides that the arrested
person must be informed of the grounds of arrest as soon as they can
be. It further provides that the arrested person has the right to defend
himself by consulting a legal practitioner of his choice. This
constitutional mandate has been effectuated by the legislature in
Section 50CrPC (now Section 47 of BNSS
